We find that the 1.3 mm map shows a morphology remarkably similar to those traced by the 22 GHz and the 7.7 µm polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission observed with JWST. The three tracers reproduce the morphology of the starburst ring with good agreement.
In particular, clumps B, C, and D are detected with similar morphology and size in the dust continuum, CO(2-1), 22 GHz, and the PAH emission.
In addition, we identify clump E (23:03:15.60 +08:52:24.56, J2000) where we detect 1.3 mm emission with a statistical significance of ∼ 18σ.

Although the bar structure is detected at a significance level of 12σ in the CO(2-1) map, it remains undetected down to 3σ in the radio continuum and in the 7.7 µm maps, despite the high angular resolution of JWST/MIRI.
We found that the majority, approximately 60%, of the SF occurs in the SB ring, consistent with Song et al. (2021).
We computed that ∼ 50% of the total cold molecular gas mass is contained in the SB ring, M(H2)_SB = (3.3 ± 1.0) × 10^9 M_⊙.

We find that the 1.3 mm map shows a morphology remarkably similar to those traced by the 22 GHz and the 7.7 µm polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission observed with JWST. The three tracers reproduce the morphology of the starburst ring with good agreement.

The overall clumps distribution appears to be consistent also with the 860 µm continuum (Izumi et al. 2020), suggesting that the 1.3 mm emission is mainly tracing thermal dust emission heated by young stars in the SB ring.
We find a stronger correlation of the PAHs with the star formation than with the CO, with steeper correlations within the starburst ring (n > 2) than in the outer region (n < 1).

Although the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the radio map is lower than that of the CO map (Section 2), the correlation between SB_PAH and Σ_SFR is stronger and narrower than that with Σ_H2. This is likely due to PAH emission being more affected by the ionizing radiation field of young stars rather than by the availability of molecular gas

Figure 4 indicates that the individual regions of NGC 7469 occupy an intermediate area of the logΣ_SFR − logΣ_H2 plane, corresponding to an intermediate star formation regime between local AGNs and U/LIRGs.

Taking advantage of interferometric mm and cm, and JWST data of nearby galaxies, it is possible to perform spatially resolved studies of the SF process in galaxies, down to hundred-parsec scales and to investigate the correlations between the PAHs, the SFR surface density (Σ_SFR) and the mass surface density of molecular gas (Σ_H2), which is the direct fuel of the formation of stars.

Due to the limitations in the current theoretical model for the JWST PSF, we do not have a robust method for removing the PSF spikes (see Williams et al. 2024, and references therein). Therefore we applied this conservative method to subtract and model the PSF contribution. We excluded from the analysis the central 1 arcsec (∼ 330 pc) region where the PSF contribution is dominant.
